---
title: broadcaster
---
## Check or Set if an Array is a Broadcaster {.unnumbered}


### Description

<code>broadcaster()</code> checks if an array or vector has the &quot;broadcaster&quot; attribute. <br />
<code>bcr()</code> is a short-hand alias for <code>broadcaster()</code>. <br />
<br />
<code style="white-space: pre;">broadcaster()&lt;-</code> (or <code style="white-space: pre;">bcr()&lt;-</code>) sets or un-sets the class attribute &quot;broadcaster&quot; on an array or vector. <br />
<br />
The <code>broadcaster</code> class attribute exists purely to overload the
arithmetic, Boolean, bit-wise, and relational infix operators,
to support broadcasting. <br />
This makes mathematical expressions with multiple variables,
where precedence may be important,
far more convenient. <br />
Like in the following calculation: <br />
<code>x / (y + z)</code> <br />
<br />
See [broadcast_operators](aaa01_broadcast_operators.qmd) for more information. <br />



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>broadcaster(x)

broadcaster(x) &lt;- value

bcr(x)

bcr(x) &lt;- value
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table role = "presentation">
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="x">x</code></td>
<td>
object to check or set. <br />
Only S3 vectors and arrays are supported, and only up to 16 dimensions.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="value">value</code></td>
<td>
set to <code>TRUE</code> to make an array a broadcaster,
or <code>FALSE</code> to remove the broadcaster class attribute from an array.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Value

For <code>broadcaster()</code>: <br />
<code>TRUE</code> if an array or vector is a broadcaster, or <code>FALSE</code> if it is not. <br />
<br />
For <code style="white-space: pre;">broadcaster()&lt;-</code>: <br />
Returns nothing,
but sets (if right hand side is <code>TRUE</code>)
or removes (if right hand side is <code>FALSE</code>)
the &quot;broadcaster&quot; class attribute. <br /> <br />



### See Also

[broadcast_operators](aaa01_broadcast_operators.qmd) <br />



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = NA}
library("broadcast")


# maths ====

x <- 1:10
y <- 1:10
dim(x) <- c(10, 1)
dim(y) <- c(1, 10)
broadcaster(x) <- TRUE
broadcaster(y) <- TRUE



x + y / x
(x + y) / x

(x + y) * x


# relational operators ====
x <- 1:10
y <- array(1:10, c(1, 10))
broadcaster(x) <- TRUE
broadcaster(y) <- TRUE

x == y
x != y
x < y
x > y
x <= y
x >= y



```
